title: Check the CLI suite is safe to run under pytest-xdist
description:
Before adding xdist, check:

- `base_checkout` is session-scoped, so it runs once per worker: is that safe and cheap?
- prek's cache under a parallel cold run (several workers populating it at once).
- `test_the_setup_helper_updates_both_layers_on_a_branch`, which failed once in the full run
  on 2026-11-23 and passed alone, possibly on the network.

Record each finding with `tp note`. Closed with --skip-verify: the outcome is the notes.
acceptance: Each of the three risks has a note saying what was found and what, if anything, changed

title: Run the CLI repo's suite on pytest-xdist, timed against the 9 minutes
description:
`uv add --dev pytest-xdist` in the CLI repo and `-n auto` in its root `addopts`. Time a cold
and a warm run against the 9 minutes, locally and on CI's 2-core runners; keep it only if it
holds up with no new flakiness, else cancel this task with the timings as the reason.

Left out on purpose: the base's own suite (~15 s) and generated projects. Worker startup eats
the gain there, the `Stop` gate would pay it every turn, and xdist breaks `breakpoint()` and
`tools/debug_pytest.py`. A project whose suite grows can add it itself; the `python-debug`
skill could then mention `-n0`.
acceptance: Cold and warm timings, local and CI, are recorded in a note
Three consecutive full runs pass with xdist on

title: Find out why Windows CI takes ten times Linux's time
description:
Unconfirmed: the uv cache is on `D:` and pytest's tmp on `C:`, so uv cannot hardlink and may
copy every package per generated project. `--basetemp` on `D:` plus `--durations=15` in a
Windows run (`gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <branch> -f windows=true`) would test it. Warm
times on 2026-10-16: Ubuntu 1m26, macOS 4m10, Windows 14m23 with the CLI suite. Closed with
--skip-verify; the finding is the note.

description:

title: DebugMCP on Windows native
description:
Unverified, and needing a session started on Windows itself: the `cmd /c` registration, `uv`
resolving as the adapter command, and both adapters launching through it, including the
`python` adapter's launcher, proven so far only on Linux. Known CLI gaps, worked around in the
`python-debug` skill rather than fixed: it ignores `launch.json`; it always sets `program`, so
pytest and every `src/` module need a launcher, and it cannot pass program arguments; complex
values render as dunder trees unless wrapped in `repr()`; the debuggee's output and logpoint
output are not captured. Closed with --skip-verify once walked.

title: Gate only changed files in a brownfield repo
description:
`finish_branch.py` runs `prek run --all-files`, and `ty` checks the whole project whatever
files it is given, so the gates fail a legacy codebase at the first save. When that reaches
`main`: a `--changed-only` flag on `finish_branch.py` reusing `stop_gate.changed_files`, and
`exclude` lists in the ty and rumdl config the adopter can edit. Also from D15: a
`bootstrap_git` question only if brownfield adoption makes `--skip-tasks` too awkward.

title: Skill lines from the spend run, on a second occurrence
description:
Act on a second occurrence, each a line in a skill: a command with more than five parameters
trips `PLR0913` and `PLR0917`, and the answer is keyword-only flags plus a commented `noqa`;
polars' `Series.sum()` is typed as a broad union, so `ty` wants `int(...)` before it reaches an
`int` parameter; a test asserting a substring of a rich table breaks when the title wraps at
80 columns.

title: Declare each setting once
description:
Only if a run shows a model fumbling "Recipe: add a setting". Today a setting is declared four
times: `Settings`, `_Overrides`, a `GlobalOptions` field or `load_settings` keyword, an option
alias; and `load_settings` copies each flag by hand. Building `given` from
`dataclasses.asdict(options)` plus the keywords, dropping `None`, deletes `_Overrides` and the
copy lines: three edits instead of four, and two wiring tests in `test_config.py` go. Bundle
with it: the app callback and each command both call `load_settings`, so every run parses the
environment and reads the config file twice; the callback needs only `verbose`. Judged not
worth changing: the unused `err` console, `config.py` importing rich through `output.py`, and
five docstring lines over 100 columns.

title: Review whether the base's _external_data defaults earn their place
description:
On `copy`, copier reads last answers from `.copier-answers.yml`, never the template's
`_answers_file`, so the base's layered copy already sees the use case's answers and the
`_external_data` defaults never decide it (found 2026-10-17). They may still serve the
standalone case and `--defaults`; decide, and simplify if not. Closed with --skip-verify.

description:

`HEAD` unless given `--vcs-ref HEAD`, so fixes stop reaching the canary until tagged. Stay
untagged until the canary settles, then the author decides.

title: Per-release update notes
description:
The README's "Keeping it in sync" covers the mechanics. A release should also say what a
conflict never will: which features were absorbed from consumers (`typer_entrypoint.py`
superseded the canary's own, with changed semantics), and which interface moves a consumer's
own commands must follow (`-v/--verbose` went global, so `tdf-cli weather -v cleve` became
`tdf-cli -v weather cleve`, and nothing warned).

title: Run the setup helper piped from the web, at a tag
description:
`curl … | sh` needs a tag or a commit in the URL, never `main`: the shim's hand-off then names
a `raw.githubusercontent.com` URL at the same ref, which `uv run` accepts. Run from a clone
only until then (D20).

title: Automate the dependency floors' updates
description:
Mostly superseded by D16: no hook rev is left to move. What is left is the dependency floors,
which drifted 10–20 releases in two months and live in each use case (the CLI template's
`uv_build>=0.12.21,<0.13.0` among them). A scheduled workflow or Renovate, gated by the
generation suite.

title: gitlab as a ci choice
description:
D17. A thin `.gitlab-ci.yml` running the same two commands as `github`, on pushes to `main`
and merge requests. Before starting, ask the author about the target instance: whether its
runners reach PyPI, GitHub and astral.sh, or need a proxy or mirror; which runner image is
allowed; whether the uv cache can be kept between jobs. Validated by hand there.

title: A seal command for downstream projects
description:
D16. A settled project runs one command that records what it runs now: an exact
`required-version`, exact `uv tool` versions for prek and copier, and the hooks' tool versions.
It runs in a generated project, never in the templates. Open: where it lives (`bootstrap.py`,
or `tools/` in the base), and how a sealed project's `copier update` keeps the seal when the
base's files move.
